outcome: Since 26 January 2024 no event has settled or moved the statement as worded: the only claimed resolution of its computational core is the Duan and Zhao programme (2019 to 2022), which predates the window and rests largely on the authors' own verdict, while the in-window events are a 2025 expository chapter that calls the problem solved, neighbouring Schubert-calculus preprints that do not touch foundations, and 2026 status pieces and a Wikipedia row that both report no consensus.
problem_asks: A rigorous foundation of Schubert calculus, in the statement's words (the calculus of Schubert's enumerative counts). Unpacked from the statement alone: (a1) the classes of the calculus and their intersection theory are rigorously defined, i.e. a foundation for the enumerative method as a whole; (a2) the multiplication rule for the calculus (products of Schubert classes) is rigorously determined, i.e. the calculus can actually be carried out. The statement names no dimension, class of varieties, special case, or algorithm, so it asks for the foundation in general. The statement does not split (a1) from (a2); they are listed separately because the literature treats them separately and an event may settle one without the other.

events.what_happened: Van der Waerden's 1930 paper in Mathematische Annalen vol. 102, pp. 337-362 (volume and pages from a Dictionary of Scientific Biography entry on Schubert and a 1936 Wirtinger citation, both via search; the Springer article page redirected to a login and was not opened, and the title was not verified). Wikipedia's Schubert-calculus section credits it with the topological foundation of the calculus. Per a search summary of van der Waerden's later 'Zur algebraischen Geometrie IV', the 1930 paper reduces the characteristics problem to computing homology of the variety viewed as a topological manifold. Wikipedia says that according to Van der Waerden and Andre Weil, Hilbert problem fifteen had been solved, 'In particular cases'.
events.delivers: A topological (homology-based) justification of the enumerative calculus, which reduces the characteristics problem to homology of the variety. Wikipedia records the credit as solving the problem only in particular cases. The 1930 text itself was not read.
events.remains: Per the later literature, the effective computation of products of Schubert classes (Schubert's problem of characteristics; Weil's problem on intersection theory of flag manifolds G/P) and the general G/P case. Not established from text read.

events.what_happened: Haibao Duan and Xuezhi Zhao, 'On Schubert's Problem of Characteristics' (arXiv:1912.10745; v1 submitted 23 Dec 2019; v2 revised 29 Oct 2020). Abstract opened (via a summarising fetch): Schubert varieties give a cell decomposition of G/P whose dual classes form an additive basis of the integral cohomology; Schubert's problem of characteristics asks how to express a monomial in these classes as a linear combination of the Schubert basis; the paper presents a unified formula for the characteristics of G/P, as polynomials in the Cartan numbers of G, and applies it to the authors' earlier Schubert-presentation work. Published in Schubert Calculus and Its Applications in Combinatorics and Representation Theory (ICTSC 2017), Springer Proceedings in Mathematics and Statistics vol. 332 (2020), pp. 43-71, per the arXiv journal reference. The abstract as read does not mention Hilbert's 15th problem.
events.revisions: v2 29 Oct 2020; published 2020 in Springer proceedings vol. 332.
events.delivers: As stated in the abstract: a unified closed formula for the characteristics of every flag manifold G/P, expressed in the Cartan numbers of G. This covers the characteristics component (expanding monomials in Schubert classes in the Schubert basis) for all G/P as the abstract claims. It does not itself claim the foundation question. Only the abstract was read; the formula and proofs were not.
events.remains: The abstract does not address the foundation part (a1), which is classical, nor state a general multiplication rule beyond the characteristics formula. The claim that the bullet as a whole is solved is made in the 2021 survey, not here.

events.what_happened: Sara C. Billey, Yibo Gao and Brendan Pawlowski, 'Introduction to the Cohomology of the Flag Variety', arXiv:2506.21064 (math.CO), submitted 26 Jun 2025 (one version, 192 pages). It is the first chapter of a planned book, Handbook of Combinatorial Algebraic Geometry: Subvarieties of the Flag Variety, edited by Erik Insko, Martha Precup and Ed Richmond. Abstract opened (via a summarising fetch): reviews how Hilbert's 15th problem has been addressed through algebraic topology, geometry and combinatorics; focuses on computation for Grassmannians and flag varieties, following Monk's constructive approach; derives formulas for Schur and Schubert polynomials; closes with open problems. Per the same fetch, the abstract says: 'Today by way of many contributions in algebraic topology, geometry, and combinatorics, we consider this solved.' and 'Yet, deep questions remain about the subtleties of actually carrying out the process.' These are quotations from a summarising fetch and must be checked against the PDF.
events.delivers: An expository survey. Its abstract states that the problem is considered solved through the contributions of algebraic topology, geometry and combinatorics, while deep questions remain about carrying out the process. It claims no new theorem about the bullet.
events.remains: By its own statement: the subtleties of actually carrying out the process (effective computation of products), with open problems listed in the chapter.
events.doubts: A survey by specialists, not a refereed verification; its 'solved' verdict is a judgement that its own abstract qualifies. Whether it cites the Duan-Zhao 2019 and 2021 texts was not checked, since the 192-page text was not read. No independent review of the chapter was found.
events.direction: A status judgement that the foundations are established, with the computational part flagged as still hard; it leans toward 'solved' in the foundations sense.

events.what_happened: David Anderson, Greta Panova and Leonid Petrov (author order on arXiv: Anderson, Panova, Petrov), 'Computation and sampling for Schubert specializations', arXiv:2603.20104 (math.CO), submitted 20 Mar 2026, one version (682 KB, 33 pages, 17 figures). Abstract opened: studies principal specialisations of Schubert polynomials (counting reduced pipe dreams); finds the first counterexample, at n = 17, to a conjecture of Merzon and Smirnov that the maximum over S_n is attained at a layered permutation; reports simulations of asymptotics; gives sampling methods. The University of Virginia news item (April 2026, opened) describes the counterexample and says 'AI-driven approaches had failed to crack' the problem; it names no system. Neighbouring: about combinatorial values of Schubert polynomials, not the foundations of Schubert calculus.
events.delivers: A counterexample to the Merzon-Smirnov conjecture on the maximal principal specialisation of Schubert polynomials, at n = 17, found by computation. It says nothing about a rigorous foundation of Schubert calculus; it concerns a combinatorial extremal question.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.directly_checkable: The counterexample is an explicit permutation in S_17. Its principal specialisation S_w(1^17) can be recomputed with the descent (Macdonald), transition (Lascoux-Schutzenberger) or cotransition (Knutson) recurrences that the paper implements. The explicit permutation was not read from the text.
events.doubts: Preprint only; no refereeing or independent recomputation was found. The result is computational.
events.direction: Counterexample to a conjecture about the same objects: the maximiser is not always a layered permutation.
events.object: The first counterexample, at n = 17, to the Merzon-Smirnov conjecture: a permutation w in S_17 whose principal specialisation of the Schubert polynomial exceeds the value at every layered permutation. Found by computation and sharper theory; the explicit permutation was not read. A specific finite object, not a non-constructive existence proof.

disputes.summary: Whether Hilbert's Problem 15 is resolved. Duan and Zhao (arXiv 2110.14989, 2021) say the 15th problem has been solved satisfactorily, an authors' verdict; Billey, Gao and Pawlowski (arXiv 2506.21064, 2025) say they consider it solved while deep questions remain about carrying out the process; Wikipedia's Hilbert's problems table (last edited 7 October 2026) says there is no consensus whether the problem is resolved completely or partially; Simons Foundation (Lamb, 18 June 2026) says there is no consensus on whether the Duan-Zhao work fully resolves it. Not resolved in this record.

Wikipedia credits van der Waerden and Weil with saying the problem had been solved, in particular cases, while the later claim of a complete solution is credited to Duan and Zhao. The 'solved' verdict is therefore attributed to different parties at different times, and the Wikipedia article itself gives no single overall verdict.

Simons (2026) and Wikipedia refer to 'the 2020 work' by Duan and Zhao. The arXiv record gives 1912.10745 as first posted December 2019 and revised October 2020, published in a 2020 Springer proceedings volume, and the survey 2110.14989 as posted in October 2021. The 2020 reference is probably the Springer volume of 1912.10745, which is inferred, not confirmed.

summary: Forty-three searches were run and 22 pages or files opened (listed under sources; several other sources, including the Springer and mathnet pages, were unreachable from this environment or were read only through search excerpts). The problem's computational core has one substantive human line of work: Duan and Zhao posted a unified formula for Schubert's problem of characteristics in December 2019 (arXiv 1912.10745; Springer proceedings 2020) and a survey in October 2021 (arXiv 2110.14989; Russian Math. Surveys 2022) that says the 15th problem has been 'solved satisfactorily', which is their own verdict; I found no independent expert check or published critique of it, and the talks restating it (2021 to 2026) add no mathematics. Both pieces predate the window. Inside the window, the only status claim of the problem itself is Billey, Gao and Pawlowski's June 2025 chapter, which calls the problem 'solved' with deep computational questions remaining; the June 2026 Simons Foundation piece and Wikipedia's October 2026 row both record no consensus. The close call is whether the Duan-Zhao claim closes the bullet: on the foundations reading (van der Waerden, Weil, Ehresmann, Chevalley, Bernstein-Gel'fand-Gel'fand per Wikipedia) the foundation was already in place by the 1950s, so only the computational residue is contested, and that residue is what Duan and Zhao claim to have closed; on the reading that treats the authors' verdict as insufficient, the record shows no consensus and no independent verification. The neighbouring in-window events are Schubert-coefficient complexity (Pak and Robichaux, December 2024), a Schubert-cell positivity theorem (Schurmann, Simpson and Wang, 2025), a Merzon-Smirnov counterexample at n = 17 (Anderson, Panova and Petrov, March 2026), a Lean formalisation of affine curve neighbourhoods (April 2026), a Grassmannian reformulation (Contiero, Gatto and Salehyan, July 2026), and two 2026 preprints with disclosed AI use on other Schubert-type problems (Pratt, 21 Sep 2026, crediting ChatGPT 5.6 Sol and Claude Fable; Hodges, 23 Sep 2026, crediting GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-6 Astra). None of these touches the foundations question. For AI involvement in this problem itself, no system was found in any source bearing on it. I checked the 10 Aug 2026 OpenAI 'ten advances' repository (none of its ten results concerns Schubert calculus) and the 6 Oct 2026 openai/math release by scanning its manuscript map (CONTENTS.md, families 001 to 377, in chunks) for Schubert, flag, enumerative, Chow, Grassmannian and Hilbert-15 titles: no match, with unrelated near-misses at families 053 and 193. A claimed AI result on Hilbert's 10th problem (arXiv 2608.31162 and the OpenAI release) is a different problem.
competing_reading: Read the bullet against the literature rather than its wording: the foundation (cohomology of G/P, Chow rings, basis theorem) was built between the 1930s and the 1950s by van der Waerden, Weil, Ehresmann, Chevalley and Bernstein-Gel'fand-Gel'fand, so the only live question is the computational residue; Duan and Zhao claim to have closed it (2019 formula, 2021 'solved satisfactorily'), and Billey, Gao and Pawlowski (2025) consider the problem solved. On that reading the problem was settled by human work before the window, nothing in the window changes that, and the 'no consensus' statements are caution rather than a finding of error.
what_would_settle_it: (1) An independent write-up or referee report checking Duan and Zhao's characteristic formula and intersection-ring system against known products on small flag manifolds (Chevalley- or Monk-type rules are natural checks); (2) the text of Remark 6.3 in arXiv 2110.14989 and the works it cites, to see what the 'solved satisfactorily' claim rests on; (3) the full text of arXiv 2506.21064, to see whether it cites the 2019 and 2021 Duan-Zhao texts and what its 'solved' verdict rests on; (4) the Springer and mathnet editorial and referee records for the 2020 and 2022 publications, which could not be reached; (5) a stated editorial position, from Wikipedia's editors or a named expert, on what 'resolved completely' would mean for this bullet.

dead_ends: No 2024 to 2026 preprint claiming a new foundation for Schubert calculus or a new resolution of Hilbert's 15th problem was found by any search.

No AI-authored or AI-assisted result on Hilbert's 15th problem or on the foundations of Schubert calculus was found (searches combining the problem with AI, LLM, GPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepMind, AlphaEvolve, AlphaProof, Erdos and Astra returned none).
OpenAI 'Ten advances' (1 August 2026): none of the ten results in the openai/ten-proofs README concerns Schubert calculus or flag manifolds.

OpenAI openai/math release (6 October 2026): CONTENTS.md read in chunks covering families 001 to 377; no title or description mentions Schubert, flag manifolds, enumerative geometry, Grassmannians, intersection theory or Hilbert's 15th problem. Near-misses only: family 053 ('A counterexample to Pixton completeness in Chow') and family 193 ('Serre's intersection-multiplicity conjecture'), both unrelated. The reading was by summarising fetch, and full manuscripts were not read.

Formal verification: no Lean or Mathlib formalisation of Schubert calculus on flag varieties or Chow rings was found; the only Lean items were the curve-neighbourhood formalisation (2604.23211) and the Hodges Theorem 1.1 formalisation.

Real Schubert calculus and machine learning (Sottile and others): nothing from 2024 to 2026 links the problem to machine learning or a conjecture; the 2023 Frontiers paper on Schubert varieties in machine learning uses the objects as data representations, not as mathematics bearing on the problem.
arXiv 2608.31162 ('Trinomial containment in polynomial ideals is undecidable'), credited to AI systems: concerns Hilbert's 10th problem, not this one.
Hilbert 16th (Buzzi-Novaes defence) and Hilbert 17th (July 2026 seminar) items: unrelated problems.
Quanta, Terence Tao and Simons coverage of Problem 15 specifically: none found.
